newsitem.title: ITALY: Relief convoys in Sierra Leone halted by ambushes.
newsitem.headline: Relief convoys in Sierra Leone halted by ambushes.

text.p: Relief convoys to eastern and southern Sierra Leone have been halted because of ambushes on food trucks, the United Nations' World Food Programme (WFP) said in a statement on Sunday.
The Rome-based agency said it feared people in the areas affected would go hungry unless the convoys resumed soon.

The WFP said rebel attacks on its trucks had been increasing since mid-August. In the latest incident, a WFP lorry was ambushed while it travelled from the Sierra Leone capital Freetown to the southern city of Bo last Wednesday.
The last food distribution in Bo was last month and there was not enough wheat to complete a full hand-out this month.
"Officials are reluctant to begin distributing food unless they have enough for everyone, fearing disturbancies from those who don't receive supplies," the WFP statement said.
The U.N. agency said around 1.5 million people in the west African country were displaced and needed food handouts to survive.
